title: Capernaum
summary: A fishing and farming settlement on the northwestern Sea of Galilee that Mark and Matthew present as a principal base for Jesus's Galilean ministry.
historical_context: Early Roman Capernaum consisted of basalt-built domestic compounds beside the lake and near regional routes. Archaeology supplies settlement context but cannot identify a particular excavated room as the house in Mark 2.
ancient_near_east_context: Capernaum belongs to the Roman-period Galilean lake economy rather than a generalized ancient Near Eastern setting.
hebraic_worldview: Homes, Sabbath assembly, healing, hospitality, and communal reputation overlap in the Gospel episodes located here.
second_temple_context: The village was a Jewish settlement in the territory of Herod Antipas during Jesus's ministry; its later monumental synagogue must not be treated as the standing building of Mark 1.
canonical_context: Mark clusters teaching, healing, controversy, and household scenes at Capernaum; Matthew calls it Jesus's own city, and John associates it with lake crossings and teaching.
literary_context: The Synoptic Gospels use repeated returns to Capernaum to connect public teaching with crowded domestic scenes, healings, disputes, and instruction of disciples.
covenantal_significance: Capernaum locates Jesus's kingdom proclamation within ordinary Jewish village life in Galilee.
canonical_role: Capernaum serves as a canonical place anchor, connecting geography, historical setting, key passages, and related people, events, and themes.
